COMPLETE VISIBLE RESPONSE (visible TeX annotations and URLs preserved):

The full question remains unresolved in this effort

I have not constructed the requested uniform deterministic strongly polynomial algorithm, and I have not proved an impossibility theorem for the full computational model. The completed work gives exact reductions, explicit representation bounds, and counterexamples to several proposed progress arguments. These do not establish the required polynomial bound on the total number of arithmetic operations.

The strongest completed result is a fully paid reduction of all three required LP outcomes to bounded certificate search, together with a precise demonstration that even a seemingly modest target-free circuit-selection operation would already solve the general problem. This identifies what the available initialization, rounding and short-walk machinery does—and what remains unconstructed.

1. Complete certificate search can be bounded and initialized within the stated model

Consider the arbitrary rational input

$$\min c^\top x \quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\qquad x\ge0.$$

There are no rank, degeneracy, coefficient-size or conditioning assumptions in the following construction.

An explicitly computable witness bound

Let

$$K=mn+m+n$$

and list all input entries as their supplied integer pairs $(p_\ell,q_\ell)$, with $q_\ell>0$. Compute

$$Q=\prod_{\ell=1}^{K}q_\ell,
\qquad
d_\ell=p_\ell
\left(\prod_{j<\ell}q_j\right)
\left(\prod_{j>\ell}q_j\right).$$

Prefix and suffix products compute these integers using $O(K)$ arithmetic operations. This uses no exact integer quotient, gcd, logarithm or floor. Access to these supplied pair fields follows the explicit implementation in Appendix A.1 of Dadush–Koh–Natura–Olver–Végh. arxiv.org [https://arxiv.org/html/2610.26073v1?utm_source=chatgpt.com]

Write the resulting integerized data as

$$C=QA,\qquad h=Qb,\qquad g=Qc.$$

Set

$$U=1+\sum_\ell |d_\ell|,\qquad
L=m+n+2,\qquad
\boxed{R=2L!U^L.}$$

The bound $R$ is computable in $O(K+L)$ operations and comparisons. Its encoding length is

$$O\!\left(L\bigl(B+\log(K+1)+\log L\bigr)\right).$$

The logarithms here describe encoding sizes; the algorithm does not evaluate them. Intermediate storage and ordinary bit work are polynomial in $(m,n,B)$.
